clue.text: Try pharmacists when suffering hangover inevitably following this?

definitions.note: the answer is the event that leads to the hangover, not a synonym for it

indicators.note: something suffering is in a bad way, knocked out of shape, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone with a hangover is advised to go and see the chemist, as the next morning always brings one.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram's suffering also suits the hangover in the surface; the definition is a descriptive phrase rather than a synonym, made fair by the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A festive office celebration in December is notorious for the heavy drinking that leaves people sore-headed the next day.

clue.text: Game tennis star loses 6-7 after speed of light ace

indicators.note: the trimmed star's name comes after the two letters for light speed and ace

parts.note: c is the physics symbol for the speed of light
A is short for ace on playing cards

indicators.note: the star's name drops its sixth and seventh letters, the last two

parts.note: Ilie Nastase was a Romanian tennis champion of the 1970s

explanation.surface: A tennis star loses a set 6-7 after being beaten by an ace served at incredible pace.
explanation.walkthrough: The 6-7 looks like a tennis score; it names letter positions, so NASTASE loses its sixth and seventh letters to leave NASTA.
explanation.definitionFit: Canasta is a rummy-style card game played with two packs, so it is an example of a game.

clue.text: Ravel opera with prominent tango as result of new arrangement

indicators.note: to ravel is to tangle, so the letters that follow are mixed up

parts.note: T is tango in the phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An opera by the composer Ravel gives a tango a prominent place.
explanation.walkthrough: Ravel looks like the French composer, and he did write a famous Boléro dance; here it is a verb that tangles the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Reapportionment is the sharing out of something again in different portions, which is what a new arrangement produces.

clue.text: Rifle bag

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to plunder or ransack a place
second meaning: a large sturdy bag

explanation.walkthrough: Rifle reads like a gun, a gun bag being a natural pairing, but it is the verb meaning to ransack.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to pillage a captured town and a large coarse container for goods.

clue.text: They were in charge of Florence Nightingale's case, dropping off supplies to hospital

definitions.text: They were in charge of Florence

indicators.note: dropping off means the named letters are taken away from the word for supplies

parts.note: medicine is what hospitals are supplied with and dispense
the case of Nightingale is its outer letters, N and E

explanation.surface: Florence Nightingale is in charge of a patient's case and falls asleep while handing out hospital supplies.
explanation.walkthrough: Florence Nightingale is the famous nurse; split them, and Florence is the Italian city, while Nightingale gives only its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Medici were the banking family who ruled the city state of Florence through much of the Renaissance.

clue.text: DC's administrator of justice fixing up America for every individual?

indicators.note: fixing means attaching, so the reversed letters are joined on to what follows
in a down clue, up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: US is short for the United States of America
per means for each, as in miles per hour
a man is an individual person

explanation.surface: A justice administrator in Washington DC is fixing up America for the benefit of every person.
explanation.walkthrough: DC looks like the District of Columbia; it is DC Comics, the publisher of the caped hero.
explanation.definitionFit: The comic-book hero published by DC fights crime and upholds truth and justice.

clue.text: Number one of all books I import is "Discovery" by Dirac

indicators.note: the number one letter of a word is its first

parts.note: NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible
import as a noun means importance, and so does matter

explanation.surface: An encyclopedia entry ranks Dirac's discovery first of all the books it brings in.
explanation.walkthrough: Paul Dirac was the physicist whose equation predicted the positron, the first antiparticle; the quotation marks admit it was a theoretical discovery.
explanation.definitionFit: Dirac's 1928 theory predicted particles with opposite charge to ordinary ones, the first sign of this mirror-image stuff.

clue.text: Pigment which blends Inuit mat colour, say, on type of leather that's not hard

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above what follows
blends means mixes, so the letters of these words are mixed together
say means as spoken, so the letters entered only sound like the word for colour

parts.note: to dye is to colour fabric

indicators.note: not means the letter for hard is left out of the leather word

parts.note: oxhide is leather made from the skin of an ox
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: An Inuit craftsman colours a mat and lays it on soft leather.
explanation.walkthrough: Colour gives DYE, and 'say' turns it into DI, which sounds the same; OXHIDE without H gives OXIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: This white compound of titanium is the most widely used white pigment in paint, plastics and sunscreen.

clue.text: Place in frame a little 22, perhaps

definitions.note: 22 is the soda clue, so this is a small amount of soda, as in whisky with a dash of it

indicators.note: in means the abbreviation for place goes inside the word for frame

parts.note: a sash is the frame holding the glass of a window
PL is the street-name abbreviation for Place

explanation.surface: An instruction to put a small amount of something in a frame.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference points at the soda answer: a splash is the little drop of soda added to a whisky.
explanation.definitionFit: A small quantity of mixer poured into a drink is called a splash, and soda is a typical example.

clue.text: Subtle letter from Makarios our church also embraces

parts.note: Makarios was a Greek Cypriot archbishop, so his letter is a Greek one, nu

indicators.note: embraces means holding something inside, so the church letters go inside the word for also

parts.note: and means also, in addition
CE is the Church of England, our church to a British setter

explanation.surface: A letter from Archbishop Makarios contains subtleties that the church takes on board too.
explanation.walkthrough: Archbishop Makarios was President of Cyprus; his name signals a Greek letter rather than a message he wrote.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nuanced has fine shades of meaning, so it is delicate and subtle rather than blunt.

clue.text: The worst and best of Heston?

definitions.note: Heston is a motorway service area on the M4 near London, an example of a stop for drivers

parts.note: the pits means the very worst
top means best, the highest

explanation.surface: Reviewing the highs and lows of the chef Heston Blumenthal.
explanation.walkthrough: Heston suggests the celebrity chef Heston Blumenthal; it is the M4 services west of London, where drivers stop for fuel and food, and the question mark flags the example.
explanation.definitionFit: A motorway services is a place for a brief halt on a long drive, which is what this phrase means outside motor racing.

clue.text: Weakens lines of defence

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to sap is to drain strength gradually
second meaning: trenches dug towards or around a fortified position

explanation.walkthrough: The military sense of saps as siege trenches is less familiar; sappers are the soldiers who dug them.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means drains of energy, and the plural noun names the trenches of siege warfare.

clue.text: Who's physical defect, a valet and primarily golden accessory?

definitions.text: Who's physical defect, a valet and primarily golden accessory?

parts.note: a scar is a mark left on the body
a man is a manservant, a valet

indicators.note: primarily means at first, so take the first letter of each of the two words

explanation.surface: A riddle asking which person is known by a bodily flaw, a manservant and a gilded accessory.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the Bond villain of The Man with the Golden Gun: he has a third nipple, a valet called Nick Nack and a golden gun.
explanation.definitionFit: Francisco Scaramanga is the assassin in Ian Fleming's novel and the 1974 film, famed for his gold pistol.

clue.text: Paganini's intoxicated by French perfume

indicators.note: someone intoxicated is all over the place, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: the violinist's name, with the apostrophe s read as is

explanation.surface: The violinist Paganini is drunk on the scent of a French perfume.
explanation.walkthrough: Niccolò Paganini was the Italian virtuoso violinist; his name supplies the letters, with the abbreviation for French added.
explanation.definitionFit: Frangipani is a perfume made from or imitating the scent of the tropical red jasmine flower.

clue.text: Glow enveloping half of rosy start to day

indicators.note: enveloping means wrapping around, so the glow word goes around the half

parts.note: an aura is a glowing light around something

indicators.note: half of means take the first two of the word's four letters

explanation.surface: A glow wraps around half of a rosy sky at daybreak.
explanation.walkthrough: The glow suggests the northern lights, another sense of the answer, but the definition is the Latin poetic word for dawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Aurora was the Roman goddess of the dawn, and her name is a poetic word for daybreak.

clue.text: Second sleeve to protect key plant

indicators.note: to protect means to surround and shield, so the key goes inside

parts.note: a bush is a metal lining sleeve in machinery, a bushing
Alt is a computer key

explanation.surface: A sleeve is used for a second to protect a key.
explanation.walkthrough: Key is the Alt key on a computer keyboard; bush is an engineering word for a tube lining a hole.
explanation.definitionFit: Saltbush is a shrub of the goosefoot family that grows on salty soils, especially in Australia.

clue.text: Retrain foremost three quarters of 15 in metropolis

indicators.note: to retrain is to train again in a new way, so these letters are rearranged
keep only the first six of the eight letters, dropping the last quarter

parts.note: 15 is the cross-reference to the plant answer at 15 across

explanation.surface: A tram network is told to retrain its leading staff in a city.
explanation.walkthrough: Six of the eight letters of the 15 across answer, plus IN, are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Istanbul is the largest city in Turkey, a vast metropolis straddling Europe and Asia.

clue.text: Is losing head in markets for equity

indicators.note: in means the trimmed word goes inside the word for markets

parts.note: fairs are markets, as in trade fairs

indicators.note: losing head means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one, so Is are ones

explanation.surface: An investor loses out in the markets while trading in equities.
explanation.walkthrough: Is looks like the verb; it is the plural of the Roman numeral I, so ONES, which loses its head to become NES.
explanation.definitionFit: Equity in its legal and moral sense means fairness and impartial justice, not shares.

clue.text: Essentially, oafish cabbie and fierce bouncer

definitions.note: a bouncer is old slang for a liar or a big lie

indicators.note: essentially means at the core, so take the two central letters of each word

explanation.surface: A boorish taxi driver and an aggressive doorman are described.
explanation.walkthrough: Bouncer suggests a nightclub doorman, matching the fierce cabbie; in older slang a bouncer is a whopping lie or one who tells it.
explanation.definitionFit: A bouncer in old slang is a teller of tall stories, which is what a liar is.

clue.text: Fix code of network — one that's scalable?

parts.note: to mend is to fix
IP is Internet Protocol, the addressing code of the internet

explanation.surface: Mending a network's code so that it can be scaled up.
explanation.walkthrough: Scalable is computer jargon for a system that can grow; here it means climbable, and the Mendips are hills in Somerset, England.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mendip is one of the Mendip Hills in south-west England, which walkers can climb.

clue.text: "Returns Only" … "Must End Shortly" (just kidding)

indicators.note: the theatre slogan is read as an instruction to cut the last letter

parts.note: a sign saying returns only outside a theatre means the show is sold out, a play full

explanation.surface: Two familiar theatre notices: only returned tickets are left, and the run closes soon.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'Returns Only' sign tells you a play is full; cut its last letter as the second notice says.
explanation.definitionFit: Playful means said in fun, which is the sense of just kidding.

clue.text: Footsie was a public disgrace!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Footsie is the nickname for the FTSE 100 share index
second meaning: the ... were a wooden frame where offenders were held to be publicly shamed

explanation.walkthrough: Footsie looks like flirting under the table; it is the London share index, and the second part describes the old punishment frame.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both company shares traded on a market and the frame in which wrongdoers were pelted in public.

clue.text: Foodies writing programs about non-vintage red that was terrible

indicators.note: about means around, so the program word goes around the rest

parts.note: bots are autonomous software programs, some of which write text
NV is the wine-list abbreviation for non-vintage
Ivan the Terrible was a Russian tsar, and red is a loose word for Russian

explanation.surface: Food lovers write software about a cheap red wine that was awful.
explanation.walkthrough: Red that was terrible looks like a wine review; it is Ivan the Terrible, with red standing for Russian, though he long predates the Soviets.
explanation.definitionFit: Bon vivants are people who enjoy good living, especially fine food and drink, much like gourmets.

clue.text: Turf accountant's first drink

parts.note: sod is a piece of turf

indicators.note: first means take the first letter of the word for accountant

explanation.surface: A bookmaker's first drink of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: Turf accountant is a jocular British name for a bookmaker; split it, and turf is SOD while accountant gives only its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Soda is a fizzy soft drink, or the soda water used as a mixer.

clue.text: Matchmaker pairs off older Romeos in the end

indicators.note: pairs off means two-letter chunks are taken from the ends of the words
in the end shows the pairs come from the final letters of each word

explanation.surface: A matchmaker sets up older lotharios as couples at last.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the last pair of letters from older and from Romeos.
explanation.definitionFit: Eros, the Greek god of love, fires the arrows that make people fall for each other, so he is a matchmaker.

clue.text: One hears you hit pauper's sole possession

indicators.note: one hears means the letters are what the spoken words sound like

parts.note: you is said like ewe, and to lam is to hit, said like lamb

explanation.surface: Someone hears the words of a person striking a poor man.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Old Testament, the prophet Nathan tells King David a parable of a rich man who takes a poor man's only ewe lamb.
explanation.definitionFit: Nathan's parable in the second book of Samuel describes the poor man owning nothing but one little female lamb.

clue.text: Club on the road returns gear for City

indicators.note: returns means goes back, so the club's letters are read backwards

parts.note: the RAC is the Royal Automobile Club, a British motoring breakdown organisation
diff is short for differential, the gearing in a car's axle

explanation.surface: A motoring club out on the road sends back some equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: The RAC is a British motoring club, like AAA; read backwards it gives CAR. The capital of Wales is the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardiff is the capital city of Wales.

clue.text: Might this supply "A1 new" fish knife material?

parts.note: read the answer as instructions: STAIN less ST leaves AIN, A1 N(ew), and STEEL less ST leaves EEL, the fish; this points at the answer

explanation.surface: A question asking whether some material could provide a new top-class fish knife.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: take ST away from STAIN and from STEEL and what is left spells A I N EEL, that is A1 N fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutlery such as table and fish knives is commonly made of chromium-alloy steel that does not rust.
